thread:
Sam (Support): Heads up — customer ACME reports sudden p99 spikes since ~09:15 UTC, dashboard shows p99 up 6x but their traced spans don't show proportional increase. Raising for oncall.
Devon (eng-oncall): Thanks Sam. Which dashboards/queries are they looking at?
Sam (Support): The /console/team/latency -> Route p99 panel (uses rollup metric: service_request_latency_bucket_rollup). Their raw traces (jaeger) show lots of 200s but a few heavy tails.
Maya (eng-sre): If rollup is misweighting samples you can get inflated p99. Can you paste the exact promQL?
Sam (Support): From dashboard JSON: 
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(service_request_latency_bucket_rollup[5m])) by (le, route))
```
They also looked at raw histogram: 
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(service_request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
```
Where rollup vs raw differ a lot.
Lia (Observability): Rollup ingestion was restarted earlier this week after a config change. There's a known sampling-weight bug in the rollup aggregator that was patched but might not have backfilled.
Devon (eng-oncall): Can we repro the discrepancy locally? Steps?
Maya (eng-sre): Quick repro: take a small dataset with many low-latency counts and a few high-latency outliers. If rollup stores only aggregated buckets without preserving sample weights, quantile histogram computation yields wrong percentiles.
Maya (eng-sre): Pseudocode: 
```
# bad rollup: sum counts by bucket but drop 'samples' weight
rollup_buckets = sum(counts)  # lost original sample_count
hist_quantile(0.99, rollup_buckets) -> inflated
```
Devon (eng-oncall): So root cause likely: rollup pipeline dropped per-bucket sample_count metadata (or normalized it incorrectly). Lia, did the recent rollup patch touch sample weighting?
Lia (Observability): Yes — the patch changed how we compress buckets to reduce storage. Compression assumed uniform weights; that was wrong. We reverted the opt in the hot path but existing rollups in object store are still wrong.
Sam (Support): Customer wants mitigation asap. They have alerts firing.
Devon (eng-oncall): Mitigations: 1) mute alerts for affected dashboard panels (temp) 2) mark rollup-derived metrics as stale/invalid in console 3) re-run corrected rollup job to backfill last 24h or at least last 2h.
Maya (eng-sre): Agree. Also add a temporary annotation to the dashboard explaining discrepancy.
Lia (Observability): I'll schedule a backfill job with corrected weighting logic. ETA ~2h for first batch (non-blocking). I'll also add a compatibility filter so new rollups are correct.
Devon (eng-oncall): I'll mute the p99 alert for their org and file an incident note. Sam, can you tell the customer we have a mitigation plan and estimate?
Sam (Support): Yep — will tell them: muting alerts, backfill in progress, expected visible fix in ~3h, followup when backfill completes.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026 | p99-rollup-weighting | priority P2 | owner: Lia (Observability).
Maya (eng-sre): Action items: Lia = backfill + patch verification; Devon = mute alerts + incident note; Sam = customer comms; me = validate post-backfill histograms vs traces.
Devon (eng-oncall): Quick note — for future, we should add a unit test that compares rollup histograms to sampled raw histograms on staging dataset to detect sample-weight skew.
Lia (Observability): Adding test and a canary job to re-run hist_comparison daily.
Sam (Support): Customer ACK'd the plan and appreciated ETA.
Maya (eng-sre): Once backfill finishes, run: 
```
# compare rollup vs raw
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(service_request_latency_bucket_rollup_corrected[5m])) by (le))
vs
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(service_request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```
and diff by route. I'll check top-10 routes.
Devon (eng-oncall): Great. Keep thread updated. If we see residual mismatch after backfill, escalate to infra for deeper ingest pipeline tracing.
Sam (Support): Updated customer with progress, they paused aggressive paging. Closing loop later. :thumbsup:
